title: CLASS 8, ICSE — Physics | Physics Topic 13
description: Subject-wise test on Physics Topic 13 (Physics) for CLASS 8, ICSE. 20Q.
subject: physics

questions.question: Which of the following is the standard SI unit of pressure?

options.explanation: Newton is the SI unit of force, not pressure.
Joule is the SI unit of energy or work, not pressure.
Pascal (Pa) is the SI unit of pressure, equivalent to N/m².
Watt is the SI unit of power, not pressure.

questions.explanation: The SI unit of force is Newton (N), of energy/work is Joule (J), and of power is Watt (W). Pressure is defined as force per unit area, and its SI unit is Pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to N/m².
questions.hint: Pressure is force divided by area.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: A force can change the: I. State of motion of an object II. Shape of an object III. Direction of motion of an object IV. Mass of an object

options.explanation: This option excludes IV, but IV is incorrect as force does not change mass.
This option excludes II, which is a valid effect of force.
Force can change the state of motion, shape, and direction of motion of an object.
IV is incorrect as force does not change the mass of an object.

questions.explanation: Force can change the speed (state of motion), shape, and direction of motion of an object. However, force does not change the mass of an object; mass is an intrinsic property.
questions.hint: Consider the effects of force on an object's motion, shape, and mass.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: A block of wood exerts a force of 100 N on a table. If the area of contact between the block and the table is 0.5 m², what is the pressure exerted by the block on the table?

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation. 100 N / 0.5 m² = 200 Pa.
Correct calculation: 100 N / 0.5 m² = 200 Pa.
Incorrect calculation. 100 N / 0.5 m² = 200 Pa.
Incorrect calculation. 100 N / 0.5 m² = 200 Pa.

questions.explanation: Pressure (P) = Force (F) / Area (A). Given: F = 100 N, A = 0.5 m². P = 100 N / 0.5 m² = 200 N/m² = 200 Pa.
questions.hint: Use the formula Pressure = Force / Area.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-contact force?

options.explanation: Frictional force is a contact force.

options.text: Muscular force applied to push a cart
options.explanation: Muscular force is a contact force.

options.text: Gravitational force acting on a falling apple
options.explanation: Gravitational force is a non-contact force.

options.text: Force applied by a spring when compressed
options.explanation: Spring force is a contact force.

questions.explanation: Non-contact forces act on an object without being in physical contact with it. Gravitational force, magnetic force, and electrostatic force are examples of non-contact forces. Frictional force, muscular force, and spring force are all contact forces.
questions.hint: Non-contact forces do not require physical touch.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Why do porters place a round piece of cloth on their heads when carrying heavy loads?

options.text: To reduce the weight of the load.
options.explanation: The weight of the load remains unchanged.

options.text: To increase the friction between the load and their head.
options.explanation: The primary purpose is to reduce pressure, not friction.

options.text: To increase the area of contact, thereby reducing the pressure on their heads.
options.explanation: Increasing the area of contact reduces pressure (P = F/A).

options.text: To provide a better grip for the load.
options.explanation: The cloth is used to reduce pressure, not improve grip.

questions.explanation: Pressure is inversely proportional to the area of contact (P = F/A). By placing a round piece of cloth, the porter increases the surface area over which the force (weight of the load) is distributed. This increase in area reduces the pressure exerted on their head.
questions.hint: Consider how increasing the area of contact affects pressure.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: An object floats in a liquid if:

options.text: Its density is equal to the density of the liquid.
options.explanation: This results in neutral buoyancy, but the object may not necessarily float.

options.text: The buoyant force is less than its weight.
options.explanation: If buoyant force is less than weight, the object sinks.

options.text: The buoyant force is greater than or equal to its weight.
options.explanation: This condition allows the object to float.

options.text: Its volume is less than the volume of the liquid.
options.explanation: Volume alone does not determine floating; density and buoyant force are key factors.

questions.explanation: An object floats if the upward buoyant force acting on it is equal to or greater than its downward weight. If the buoyant force is less than its weight, the object sinks. If its density is equal to the liquid's density, it floats just below the surface (neutral buoyancy).
questions.hint: Consider the balance between buoyant force and weight.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Atmospheric pressure is highest at:

options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude.
Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude.
Atmospheric pressure is highest at sea level.

options.text: In an airplane flying at 10,000 meters
options.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude.

questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the column of air above a given point. The column of air is densest and tallest at sea level, hence atmospheric pressure is highest at sea level and decreases as altitude increases.
questions.hint: Consider where the air column is densest and tallest.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Two forces, F1 = 15 N acting towards the East and F2 = 20 N acting towards the West, are applied to an object. What is the net force acting on the object?

options.explanation: Net force = 20 N (West) - 15 N (East) = 5 N (West).
Incorrect addition of forces in opposite directions.
Incorrect addition of forces in opposite directions.
Incorrect direction of net force.

questions.explanation: Forces acting in opposite directions are subtracted. Net force = 20 N (West) - 15 N (East) = 5 N (West).
questions.hint: Subtract the smaller force from the larger force in opposite directions.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements about pressure is INCORRECT?

options.text: Pressure increases with depth in a liquid.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about pressure in liquids.

options.text: Pressure exerted by fluids is transmitted equally in all directions.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about fluid pressure (Pascal's Law).

options.text: The pressure exerted by a solid object depends only on the force applied and not on the area of contact.
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect. Pressure depends on both force and area (P = F/A).

options.text: Atmospheric pressure can crush a tin can if the air inside is removed.
options.explanation: This is a correct statement about atmospheric pressure.

questions.explanation: Pressure exerted by a solid object is defined as Force/Area (P=F/A). Therefore, it depends not only on the force applied but also crucially on the area of contact. A smaller area of contact results in higher pressure for the same force. Statements A, B, and D are correct principles of pressure.
questions.hint: Consider the formula for pressure and its dependencies.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: A syringe works on the principle of:

options.explanation: Buoyancy is not the principle behind a syringe.
Gravitational force is not the principle behind a syringe.
A syringe works by creating a pressure difference to draw in or expel liquid.
Magnetic force is not the principle behind a syringe.

questions.explanation: A syringe operates by creating a pressure difference. When the plunger is pulled back, it increases the volume inside the barrel, reducing the pressure. The higher atmospheric pressure outside then pushes the liquid into the syringe. When the plunger is pushed forward, it increases the pressure inside, expelling the liquid.
questions.hint: Consider how a syringe creates movement of liquid.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Which of the following is the SI unit of pressure?

options.explanation: Joule is the SI unit of energy.
Newton is the SI unit of force.
Pascal is the SI unit of pressure.
Watt is the SI unit of power.

questions.explanation: The SI unit of pressure is Pascal (Pa), which is equivalent to Newtons per square meter (N/m²). Joule is the unit of energy, Newton is the unit of force, and Watt is the unit of power.
questions.hint: Think about the units related to force and area.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: A car travels a distance of 180 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed in meters per second (m/s)?

options.explanation: Incorrect calculation.
Incorrect calculation.
Correct calculation.
Incorrect calculation.

questions.explanation: Distance = 180 km = 180 * 1000 m = 180000 m. Time = 3 hours = 3 * 60 * 60 s = 10800 s. Average Speed = Distance / Time = 180000 m / 10800 s ≈ 16.67 m/s.
questions.hint: Convert kilometers to meters and hours to seconds before calculating speed.

questions.question: An object floats in a liquid if:

options.text: Its density is greater than the density of the liquid.
options.explanation: This would cause the object to sink.

options.text: Its weight is greater than the buoyant force.
options.explanation: For floating, weight must equal buoyant force.

options.text: Its density is less than the density of the liquid.
options.explanation: This is the condition for an object to float.

options.text: Its volume is equal to the volume of the liquid displaced.
options.explanation: This is a property of floating objects but not the defining condition.

questions.explanation: An object floats if its average density is less than the density of the fluid it is immersed in. If the density of the object is greater, it sinks. The buoyant force acting on an object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced. For floating, the buoyant force must be equal to the weight of the object, which implies the object's density is less than or equal to the liquid's density.
questions.hint: Consider the relationship between the object's density and the liquid's density.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of chemical energy being converted into light energy?

options.text: A solar panel converting sunlight into electricity.
options.explanation: This converts light energy to electrical energy.
This converts chemical energy to light and heat energy.

options.text: A light bulb glowing when electricity passes through it.
options.explanation: This converts electrical energy to light energy.

options.text: A fan rotating when switched on.
options.explanation: This converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.

questions.explanation: When a candle burns, the wax (a chemical substance) undergoes a combustion reaction, releasing energy in the form of heat and light. This is a direct conversion of chemical energy to light and heat. Solar panels convert light to electrical, light bulbs convert electrical to light, and fans convert electrical to mechanical.
questions.hint: Look for a process involving a chemical reaction producing light.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: When a ray of light passes from a rarer medium (like air) to a denser medium (like glass) and strikes the boundary at an angle, it:

options.explanation: This happens when light moves from denser to rarer medium.
This is the correct behavior when light moves from rarer to denser medium.
This only happens if the angle of incidence is zero or the media have the same refractive index.

options.text: Reflects back into the rarer medium.
options.explanation: This is reflection, not refraction.

questions.explanation: According to the laws of refraction, when light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, its speed decreases, and it bends towards the normal. Conversely, from denser to rarer, it bends away from the normal.
questions.hint: Recall the behavior of light during refraction between different media.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: In a series circuit containing three identical bulbs, what happens to the overall brightness of the remaining bulbs if one of the bulbs fuses (breaks)?

options.explanation: The circuit is broken, so no current flows.

options.text: The remaining bulbs glow with the same brightness.
options.explanation: The circuit is broken, so no current flows.
The circuit is broken, so no current flows.

options.text: Only the bulb immediately next to the fused bulb goes out.
options.explanation: The entire circuit is broken, so all bulbs go out.

questions.explanation: In a series circuit, components are connected end-to-end, forming a single path for current. If one bulb fuses, it breaks the circuit, creating an open path. Consequently, no current can flow through any part of the circuit, causing all other bulbs to go out.
questions.hint: Consider how current flows in a series circuit and the effect of a broken component.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: The characteristic of sound that helps us distinguish between a loud sound and a faint sound, even if they have the same pitch, is:

options.explanation: Pitch depends on frequency.
Quality helps distinguish between different sound sources.
Loudness depends on amplitude.
Frequency determines pitch.

questions.explanation: Loudness is the characteristic of sound that depends on its amplitude and allows us to distinguish between loud and faint sounds. Pitch depends on frequency, and quality (timbre) helps distinguish between different sound sources producing the same pitch and loudness.
questions.hint: Think about what changes when a sound becomes louder or fainter.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-contact force?

options.explanation: Frictional force requires physical contact.
Muscular force requires physical contact.
Magnetic force acts at a distance.
Normal force requires physical contact.

questions.explanation: Non-contact forces are forces that act on an object without coming physically in contact with it. Magnetic force (and gravitational force, electrostatic force) are examples of non-contact forces. Frictional, muscular, and normal forces all require physical contact.
questions.hint: Consider forces that act at a distance without physical touch.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: Two identical metal spheres, A and B, are at temperatures of 70°C and 30°C respectively. When they are brought into thermal contact, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Heat flows from B to A until both reach 100°C.
options.explanation: Heat flows from higher to lower temperature.

options.text: Heat flows from A to B until both reach 0°C.
options.explanation: Heat flows until thermal equilibrium, not to 0°C.

options.text: Heat flows from A to B until both reach a common intermediate temperature.
options.explanation: This is the correct behavior.

options.text: Heat flows equally in both directions, so no net change occurs.
options.explanation: Heat flows from higher to lower temperature until equilibrium.

questions.explanation: Heat always flows from a region of higher temperature to a region of lower temperature until thermal equilibrium is reached, meaning both objects attain a common intermediate temperature. In this case, sphere A is hotter (70°C) than sphere B (30°C), so heat will flow from A to B until they reach the same temperature, which will be somewhere between 30°C and 70°C (assuming no heat loss to surroundings).
questions.hint: Recall the direction of heat flow and the concept of thermal equilibrium.
questions.subject: physics

questions.question: An electromagnet works on the principle that:

options.text: Magnets attract all types of metals.
options.explanation: This is a property of magnets, not the principle of an electromagnet.
Electric current does not always generate light.

options.text: Electric current produces a magnetic field.
options.explanation: This is the principle behind an electromagnet.

options.text: Magnetic fields can generate electric current.
options.explanation: This describes electromagnetic induction, not the working of an electromagnet.

questions.explanation: An electromagnet is a temporary magnet created when electric current flows through a coil of wire (usually around a ferromagnetic core). This demonstrates the magnetic effect of electric current, where the current produces a magnetic field. Option D describes electromagnetic induction, which is a related but different principle for generating current.
questions.hint: Think about how an electromagnet is created and what causes it to work.
